title: ECC-Protected Sensor Data Memory on the AMD AUP ZU3
summary: Memories in real electronic systems are not perfect. Radiation, voltage noise and ageing can flip stored bits (*soft errors*). Automotive, aerospace, medical and server systems therefore protect their memories with an ECC: extra check bits are stored next to the data, so that when a word is read, a single flipped bit can be **corrected** and a double flip **detected**. The same idea protects DDR memory in servers, caches in processors and on-chip memories in safety-critical FPGAs and ASICs.
tools: AMD AUP ZU3 board (Zynq UltraScale+ MPSoC), Vivado (incl. Vivado Simulator), Vitis
prerequisites: Digital logic and FSMs, an HDL (Verilog/SystemVerilog), C programming, basic probability
goals: **Select and specify the sensors:** choose the sensor chips to emulate (at least two, with different buses) and write a short specification of each emulator from the real datasheet.

**Design the RTL** in SystemVerilog: sensor emulators, I²C and SPI masters, sample packer, (39,32) SECDED encoder and decoder, ECC-protected BRAM ring buffer, fault injection and an AXI4-Lite register interface.
**Verify each module** with its own self-checking testbench (unit level), including assertions on the bus protocols.
**Verify the top-level design** with a class-based, constrained-random SystemVerilog environment with a scoreboard, assertions and functional coverage; reach the coverage goals of “Coverage goals”.
**Prove the ECC behaviour:** 100% of injected single-bit errors corrected and 100% of injected double-bit errors detected, in simulation and on the board.
**Integrate with the Zynq PS:** synthesize and implement the design for the AUP ZU3 with no timing violations, and read the stored samples and error counters from a Vitis application.
outcomes: read a sensor datasheet and turn it into an RTL specification and register map;
design synthesizable SystemVerilog with clear interfaces, FSMs and parameterised modules;
explain and implement Hamming SECDED encoding and decoding;
build a layered, class-based SystemVerilog testbench with constrained-random stimulus, a scoreboard, SVA and functional coverage, and run a regression;
integrate custom RTL with the Zynq PS over AXI4-Lite and write a bare-metal Vitis application;
close timing and analyse resource usage in Vivado.
